title: Moroccan Carrot and Orange Salad
subtitle: Grated carrot and orange segments with cumin, cinnamon and fresh coriander
excerpt: A bright Moroccan salad of finely grated carrot with orange segments and a lightly spiced dressing of cumin, cinnamon, lemon and olive oil. Takes ten minutes and keeps well all day.
sourceNotes: Carrot salad with cumin (khoizou) is a staple of the Moroccan table, appearing at most traditional meals as part of a spread of cold salads (salatas). The combination of raw carrot with citrus, cumin and olive oil is documented throughout Moroccan and North African cookbooks. It spread to British and French cooking through the influence of writers such as Claudia Roden and Paula Wolfert, and is now a widely recognised North African classic.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Stir before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made at least 20 minutes ahead to let the spices bloom into the carrot.

content.text: Moroccan carrot salad is ten minutes of work and keeps all day. It relies on finely grated rather than coarsely grated carrot: the fine threads absorb the dressing better and have a lighter, less crunch-dominant texture. The cumin and cinnamon in the dressing are warm without being strong; the orange and lemon provide acid. Leave for at least 20 minutes before serving.

items.prepNote: peeled and segmented, or flesh only squeezed to juice
leaves and thin stems, roughly chopped

content.text: Place the finely grated carrot in a large bowl. Add the orange segments or stir in the orange juice. Whisk together the lemon juice, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{cumin-ground}} of ground cumin, {{cinnamon-ground}} of ground cinnamon, {{honey}} of honey, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour the dressing over the carrot and toss well. Leave for 20 minutes, then toss again. Scatter over the {{coriander}} of coriander just before serving.

items.cause: Carrot releases liquid as it sits with the dressing.
items.fix: This is normal. Drain off any excess liquid before serving if it has pooled, or increase the grated carrot slightly to absorb it.

items.cause: Spices added in excess or not left to bloom.
items.fix: The 20-minute rest is not optional; the cumin softens considerably as it sits in the citrus and oil. Start with the amounts in the recipe and taste before adjusting.

content.text: Carrot salad with cumin and orange is a staple of the Moroccan table, served as one of a spread of salads at most traditional meals. It came to British and French cooking through writers who wrote about Moroccan food from the 1960s. It is one of the simplest spiced salads and works alongside lamb, chicken or falafel.
